tools.name: add_redaction
tools.description: Add a user-drawn redaction bar on a page at a page-relative rectangle (fractions of the page, origin top-left). The page repaints. Returns the new id and counts. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

tools.name: describe_capabilities
tools.description: Describe the in-page Cover redaction engine for an agent: what it detects, what it refuses, how a document gets onto the page, what the tools return and what they never return. Read this first. Privacy: the document is processed inside this browser tab (WebAssembly); nothing is uploaded and the document never leaves the page. These tools return counts, ids, categories, state and page-relative geometry only — never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

tools.name: finalize
tools.description: Bake the current redaction set into the ORIGINAL document (edited sets go through the engine's apply-rects; an untouched set is the engine's own output) and hand the redacted PDF to the person through the page's download. The file goes to their machine, never through this tool: the result carries filename, byte size, page count, the number of active redactions, and watermark (whether the engine stamped THIS file). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

tools.name: get_redaction_result
tools.description: The result of the engine run on one document: redacted (true/false), status, counts by category (detections and painted bars), tier, names_checked, not_covered, watermark, timings and the event log. It RETURNS PROMPTLY and is meant to be POLLED IN A LOOP: it blocks at most 10 seconds, then returns status "pending" with retry_after_s and a next_step. Pending is NOT a failure and NOT a reason to stop. A first run on a fresh browser needs roughly 60 seconds in total (nearly all of it a one-time ~265 MB name-model download), so EXPECT ABOUT 6 TO 8 CALLS. Do not try to cover that with one long wait - timeout_s is capped at 10 and a longer request is clamped. status is "done" or "refused" when it is final. A refused document returns {error: "needs_ocr" | "encrypted_unsupported", next_step}. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

wait.description: Wait for the run to finish (default true).

wait_for_names.description: When waiting, wait for the names tier too, not just the structured tier (default true).

timeout_s.description: Seconds to block before returning status "pending" (default 10, max 10). This tool NEVER blocks longer than that: poll it repeatedly instead of asking for one long wait.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Where things stand: engine readiness, whether the names tier is enabled, and every document on the page with its document_id, name, page count, state (queued | running | done | refused), stage (waiting | structured | names | done; edits need names or done), refusal (error code + next step), detections by category, names_checked, watermark and a short structured event log per document (its milestones plus the latest two entries; bar tallies, timings and the fuller log are on get_redaction_result). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

include_events.description: Include each document's event log (default true).

tools.name: list_redactions
tools.description: Every redaction on a document as the editor holds it right now: id, page (1-based), category (e.g. US_SSN, PERSON; null for a drawn bar), origin (engine | user), active (false = an engine detection the editor turned off), and its rectangle as page-relative fractions. Ids: "e<n>" engine, "u<n>" user-drawn; engine ids are reissued when the names tier lands (see revision). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

page.description: Only this page (1-based). Default: all pages.

tools.name: load_sample_document
tools.description: Put this page's own built-in sample document on the page, as if a person had dropped it, and return its document_id. For a HEADLESS run: the tools take their input from a human hand, so on a page nobody has dropped a file onto, every other document tool has nothing to act on and get_status returns an empty list. This is the way in. It takes NO input - not file bytes, not a URL, not a path - and always loads the SAME fixed document: a synthetic residential lease agreement (one page) that this site already publishes. It cannot be pointed at anything else, so it is not a way to get a document into this page from outside. Calling it twice adds a second copy rather than replacing the first; call get_status if you are unsure whether one is already loaded. It never counts against the daily document limit, so it cannot be refused with daily_limit however many times it is loaded. It returns immediately; the document then REDACTS IN THE BACKGROUND and takes about 60 seconds to finish on a fresh browser (a one-time ~265 MB name-model download, not the redaction itself). Poll rather than assuming it failed. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

tools.name: redact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: the engine reads the value under that bar (in-page; it is never returned) and redacts every other occurrence of it across the document, on every page. Returns only the number of bars added. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.

tools.name: remove_category
tools.description: Turn off every active engine redaction of one category (e.g. PERSON, US_ADDRESS) on a document. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

category.description: A category name as returned by list_redactions / get_redaction_result counts.

tools.name: remove_redactions
tools.description: Turn the given redactions off (an engine detection becomes inactive and can be restored; a user-drawn bar is deleted). The page repaints so the person watching sees the change. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

tools.name: restore_category
tools.description: Turn every inactive engine redaction of one category back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

category.description: A category name as returned by list_redactions / get_redaction_result counts.

tools.name: restore_redactions
tools.description: Turn inactive engine redactions (ids "e<n>") back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

tools.name: unredact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool in reverse, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: every other active redaction of the same value across the document is turned off. The keyed bar itself stays. Returns only the number turned off. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.
